summary: @servicetitan/testing-library preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13) for the current platform/arch, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, then invokes it as `bun math_init.js` against a sibling file bundled with the package. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun CJS bundle with rotating string-array obfuscation (hex identifiers, alphabet-based decoder, numeric token arrays) that does not correspond to any source in src/ and is not built from the visible React testing helpers. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern — fetching a second language runtime at install and handing it an opaque sibling payload — causes arbitrary code to execute on the installer's machine at `npm install` under a runtime that bypasses Node-based scanners. A React testing library has no legitimate need to bootstrap a second runtime or to ship a 700KB obfuscated Bun binary payload; the shape and purpose-mismatch are consistent with a loader/stealer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
